examples.en: The trailer for the new movie was released yesterday.
The exam results will be made public next week.
Personal information must not be made public.
I was shocked that the secret photo was posted online.
Everyone is waiting for the day it's revealed.

examples.ko: 새 제품은 내년 봄에 공개될 거예요.
examples.en: The new product will be unveiled next spring.

explain: '공개하다'는 내보이는 쪽, '공개되다'는 숨겨져 있던 것이 보이게 되는 쪽이에요. 반대말은 '비공개'예요. 영화·제품·정보·사진에 두루 쓰고, 구어에서는 '오픈되다'도 들려요. '발표되다'는 공식적으로 알린다는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: The new photo was made public this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 이미 모두에게 보여졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense: it has already been shown to everyone.

phrases.en: That information hasn't been made public yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 알려지지 않았다는 것을 말하는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form saying it is not yet publicly known.

phrases.example: 이 사진은 누구나 볼 수 있게 공개돼 있어요.
phrases.en: This photo is open to everyone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 있다'를 붙여 지금 공개된 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 있다' describes the current open state.

explain_en: '공개하다' is showing it; '공개되다' is something hidden coming into view. The opposite is '비공개'. It works for movies, products, information and photos, and in casual speech you may hear '오픈되다' too. '발표되다' has a stronger feel of an official announcement.

examples.en: Incheon International Airport is really big and clean.
It takes an hour by bus to get to the international airport.
My hometown Busan also has an international airport.

examples.ko: 저는 김포 국제공항에서 친구를 두 시간 기다렸어요.
examples.en: I waited two hours for my friend at Gimpo International Airport.

examples.ko: 새 국제공항이 내년 봄에 문을 열어요.
examples.en: A new international airport opens next spring.
There are many hotels near the international airport.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '공항'이라고만 해도 충분해요. '국제공항'은 공항 이름이나 뉴스, 안내문에서 자주 보여요. 해외로 가는 비행기는 '국제선', 나라 안에서 타는 비행기는 '국내선'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Let's meet at the airport tomorrow morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '국제공항'보다 짧고 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter and much more common in daily conversation.

phrases.en: I arrive at the international airport at eight in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비행기나 차로 공항에 닿는다는 뜻으로 안내문이나 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in announcements and news for arriving at the airport.

phrases.en: How long does it take to get to the international airport by taxi?
phrases.nuance_ko: '까지'를 붙여 공항까지 가는 거리나 시간을 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 까지 you ask about the distance or time to reach the airport.
phrases.en_equiv: as far as the international airport

explain_en: In everyday talk just '공항' (airport) is enough. 'Gukje gonghang' shows up in airport names, news and signs. Flights abroad are '국제선' (international) and domestic ones are '국내선'.

examples.en: I finally return to my home country next month.
My friend came back from the United States yesterday.
When do you plan to return home after you finish studying abroad?
I slept the whole way on the flight home.
As soon as I got home, I went to see my family.
After returning home, I found a new job.

explain: 외국에 있다가 자기 나라로 돌아올 때 써요. '입국하다'는 어느 나라든 그 나라에 들어올 때 쓰는 말이라 외국인에게도, 돌아오는 한국 사람에게도 써요. 반대말은 나라를 떠나는 '출국하다'예요.

phrases.en: I'll contact you right after I return to my country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌아온 뒤의 일을 말할 때 조건처럼 이어서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links to what happens once you return.

phrases.en: The date of return hasn't been decided yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 나라로 돌아오는 날을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the day of returning to your country.

phrases.en: I miss home, so I want to return soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌아오고 싶은 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses the wish to come back to your country.

explain_en: Use it when you come back to your own country from abroad. '입국하다' is used for entering any country, so it applies to foreigners as well as Koreans coming home. The opposite is '출국하다', leaving the country.

en: being on duty; one's turn; shift

examples.en: Today I'm on cleaning duty.

examples.ko: 청소 당번은 순번을 정해서 돌아가며 맡기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to set an order and take turns on cleaning duty.

examples.ko: 다음 주 급식 당번을 정하는 중이에요.
examples.en: We're deciding who has lunch duty next week.
Whoever is on duty, please erase the board.

examples.ko: 저는 이번 주 당번이 아니라서 먼저 갈게요.
examples.en: I'm not on duty this week, so I'll head out first.
In the duty order, I come right after my friend.

explain: 학교나 직장에서 돌아가며 맡는 일에 써요. '청소 당번', '급식 당번'처럼 앞에 일을 붙이고, '당번을 서다/맡다/바꾸다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: Who is on cleaning duty this week?
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 일을 붙여 무슨 당번인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the task in front to say what duty it is.

phrases.en: I took the duty this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 일을 책임지고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you take responsibility for it.

phrases.en: I swapped duty days because I have something tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람과 순서를 바꿀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when swapping turns with someone.

explain_en: It is used for jobs people take in turns at school or work. Put the task in front, as in '청소 당번' or '급식 당번', and say '당번을 서다/맡다/바꾸다'.

examples.en: I bought a new domain for my website.
The shorter a domain name is, the easier it is to remember.

examples.ko: 우리 가게 도메인이 아직 사용 가능한지 확인해 봤어요.
examples.en: I checked whether our shop's domain is still available.
I send emails from the company domain.

examples.ko: 도메인 주소가 바뀌어서 접속이 안 돼요.
examples.en: The domain address changed, so I cannot connect.

examples.ko: 이 도메인은 이미 다른 사람이 쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: Someone else is already using this domain.

explain: 도메인은 '사다', '등록하다'와 자주 같이 써요. 영어 domain을 그대로 읽은 외래어예요. 인터넷 주소 전체는 '주소'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I bought a domain to make a shop website.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인터넷 주소 이름을 쓸 권리를 얻을 때 '사다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '사다' is used when you get the right to use a web address name.

phrases.en: What should we use for the domain name?
phrases.nuance_ko: 인터넷 주소에 들어가는 이름을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name that goes into a web address.

phrases.en: I registered a domain under the company name.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주소를 정식으로 신청해서 쓰게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you officially sign up to use an address.

explain_en: 도메인 often goes with '사다' and '등록하다'. It is the English word domain read in Korean. The whole web address is just called '주소'.

examples.en: Next Wednesday is election day.
Schools are closed on election day.
There are only three days left until election day.

examples.ko: 선거일을 잊지 않으려고 달력에 적어 두었어요.
examples.en: I wrote election day on the calendar so I would not forget.

examples.ko: 선거일 전날에는 거리에 포스터가 많이 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: The day before election day, many posters are up on the streets.
Election day is a public holiday, so many people take the day off.

explain: 생일, 휴일, 기념일처럼 '-일'은 특별한 날 이름 뒤에 붙는 끝말이에요. '선거일'은 한 단어로 붙여 써요. '선거일이 다가오다', '선거일에 투표하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I woke up early on voting day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '선거일'과 거의 같고, 투표하는 날을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as '선거일', but stresses the day you vote.

phrases.en: Election day is getting close, so the streets are noisy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날짜가 가까워질 때 '다가오다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '다가오다' when the date is getting near.

phrases.en: I went to the polling place on the morning of election day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선거일 안의 시간을 말할 때 뒤에 '아침'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add a time like '아침' to say when on election day.

explain_en: Like '생일', '휴일' and '기념일', the ending '-일' attaches to the name of a special day. Write '선거일' as one word. It goes with phrases like '선거일이 다가오다' and '선거일에 투표하다'.

examples.ko: 앞일은 아무도 모르니까 너무 걱정하지 마세요.
examples.en: No one knows what lies ahead, so don't worry too much.
When I think about what's ahead, I can't sleep.
He invested while looking far ahead into the future.
The future felt hopeless, so I talked it over with my parents yesterday.

examples.ko: 졸업하고 나서 앞일을 같이 의논해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's discuss what comes next together after we graduate.
You can think about what's next when the time comes.

explain: '미래'보다 일상적인 말이고, 내가 앞으로 겪을 일을 걱정하거나 기대할 때 써요. '앞일이 걱정되다, 앞일을 내다보다, 앞일을 알 수 없다'처럼 짝이 되는 표현이 많아요. 지나간 일은 '지난 일'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I'm worried about what's ahead, so I can't sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로의 일이 불안할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when feeling anxious about what lies ahead.

phrases.example: 앞일을 알 수 없으니까 지금 열심히 살아요.
phrases.en: I can't know what's ahead, so I do my best right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미래를 알 수 없다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to mean the future is unknowable.

phrases.en: Sometimes I feel lost when I think about what lies ahead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 일어날 일을 떠올릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when thinking about what will happen in the future.

explain_en: It is more everyday than '미래' (future) and is used when you worry about or look forward to what you will go through. Common pairings are '앞일이 걱정되다', '앞일을 내다보다' and '앞일을 알 수 없다'. Things that have already passed are '지난 일'.

examples.en: My grandmother is in a room on the third floor.

examples.ko: 입원실이 조용해서 푹 쉴 수 있어요.
examples.en: The hospital room is quiet, so I can rest well.

examples.ko: 입원실에서는 큰 소리로 전화하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not talk loudly on the phone in the patient room.
The hospital bed was uncomfortable, so I slept badly.
The nurse brought my medicine to the room.
I told them I'd like to change rooms.

explain: '병실'도 같은 뜻으로 써요. 입원실은 병원 안내문이나 서류에서 많이 보이는 말이에요. 여러 사람이 함께 쓰는 방은 '다인실', 혼자 쓰는 방은 '1인실'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: My father is in the hospital room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른이 있다고 높여 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to politely say an elder is there.

phrases.en: The hospital room is clean and quiet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '입원실'과 같은 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the same meaning as '입원실'.

phrases.en: It's a single room, so I can rest comfortably.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혼자 쓰는 입원실을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A hospital room used by one person.

explain_en: '병실' means the same thing. '입원실' is a word you often see in hospital notices and paperwork. A shared room is '다인실' and a private room is '1인실'.

examples.ko: 세 번째 정류소를 지날 때까지 우리는 말없이 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: We sat in silence until we passed the third stop.

examples.ko: 집 앞 정류소에서 오 분만 기다리면 버스가 와요.
examples.en: If you wait just five minutes at the stop in front of my house, a bus comes.
The next stop is our school.
There is a convenience store near the stop, so it's convenient.
Arrival times are shown at every stop.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 정류소 지붕 아래에 서 있었어요.
examples.en: It was raining, so I stood under the roof of the stop.

explain: '정류장'과 같은 곳을 가리켜요. '정류소에서 기다리다', '정류소에서 내리다'처럼 '에서'와 함께 많이 써요. '버스 정류소'처럼 앞에 '버스'를 붙이면 더 분명해요.

phrases.en: I decided to meet my friend at the bus stop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정류소'와 같은 뜻이고, 일상 대화에서는 '정류장'을 더 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same thing, and 'jeongnyujang' is more common in everyday talk.

phrases.en: The bus stop is close to my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: '버스'를 붙이면 어떤 정류소인지 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'bus' makes it clear what kind of stop you mean.

phrases.en: I will get off at the next stop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 버스 안에서 내릴 곳을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase on the bus when saying where you will get off.

explain_en: It refers to the same place as '정류장'. It is often used with '에서', as in '정류소에서 기다리다' or '정류소에서 내리다'. Adding '버스' in front, as in '버스 정류소', makes it clearer.

en: to get confused; to become disordered; to descend into chaos

examples.en: They're twins, so I get confused about who is who.
The roads were complicated, so I lost my sense of direction.
Similar words keep confusing me, which is hard.

examples.ko: 날짜가 헛갈리지 않게 달력에 적어 두세요.
examples.en: Write it on the calendar so you don't mix up the dates.

examples.ko: 두 사람 이름이 헛갈릴 때가 있어요.
examples.en: There are times I mix up the two people's names.

examples.ko: 설명이 너무 어려워서 더 헛갈리는 것 같아요.
examples.en: The explanation is so hard that I think it's confusing me even more.

explain: '헷갈리다'로도 쓰고 둘 다 맞는 말이에요. 두 가지가 비슷해서 구별이 안 되거나 정신이 혼란스러울 때 써요. '헷갈려요'가 입에 더 익숙하다고 느끼는 사람도 많아요.

phrases.en: The two words are similar, so I get them mixed up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '헛갈리다'와 같은 뜻이고 말할 때 더 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 헛갈리다, and heard more often in speech.

phrases.en: Write down the confusing words separately.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 뒤의 말을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -는 to modify the noun that follows.

phrases.en: I marked it with colors so it wouldn't be confusing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혼동을 피하려고 무언가 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when doing something to avoid confusion.
phrases.en_equiv: so as not to get confused

explain_en: It can also be written '헷갈리다', and both forms are correct. Use it when two things are similar and hard to tell apart, or when your mind is muddled. Many people find '헷갈려요' more familiar to say.

en: by any chance; if by some chance

examples.ko: 혹 길을 잃으면 이 번호로 전화하세요.
examples.en: If you happen to get lost, call this number.

examples.ko: 혹 제가 잘못 들었다면 다시 말해 주세요.
examples.en: If I happened to hear it wrong, please say it again.

examples.ko: 혹 내일 시간이 되면 같이 가요.
examples.en: If you happen to have time tomorrow, let's go together.
If I happen to be late, please start first.
If it should rain, take an umbrella.

examples.ko: 혹 질문이 있으면 편하게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: If you happen to have a question, feel free to ask.

explain: '혹시'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 더 글 같은 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '혹시'를 써요. '혹'은 '혹 ~(으)면'처럼 조건 앞에 오고, '혹은'(=또는)은 다른 말이에요. 몸에 난 '혹'도 소리만 같은 다른 단어예요.

phrases.en: Do you by any chance have time now?
phrases.nuance_ko: '혹'과 뜻이 같지만 일상 대화에서 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 혹, but much more common in everyday speech.

phrases.en: Just in case it rains, use an umbrella.
phrases.nuance_ko: '혹시'보다 만약의 경우를 더 강조할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stresses the unlikely 'just in case' more strongly than 혹시.
phrases.en_equiv: just in case; if by any chance

phrases.en: I left early in case I'd be late.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일이 생길까 걱정되어 미리 하는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something you do ahead of time because you worry something bad might happen.

explain_en: It means about the same as '혹시' but sounds more bookish; in everyday conversation people usually say '혹시'. '혹' comes before a condition, as in '혹 ~(으)면', and '혹은' (meaning 'or') is a different word. The lump on the body, '혹', only sounds the same.

en: to be checked; to be confirmed; to be verified

examples.en: The cause of the accident hasn't been confirmed yet.
The name and address on the application have both been verified.
When the reservation is confirmed, I'll send you a text.
An error was found, so we fixed the app again.
The news says a new fact has been confirmed.
I'll tell you as soon as it's confirmed.

explain: '확인하다'는 내가 맞는지 보는 것이고, '확인되다'는 확인한 결과가 나온 상태예요. 뉴스·공지·보고서에서 '~로 확인됐다'라는 표현을 자주 봐요. 아직이면 '확인되지 않았어요', 또는 '미확인'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I'll tell you only the confirmed information.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여 이미 확인된 것을 꾸며 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use -ㄴ to describe something that has already been confirmed.

phrases.en: Please let me know right away when the result is confirmed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)면'을 붙여 확인된 뒤에 할 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -(으)면 to say what to do once it is confirmed.

phrases.en: That person was confirmed to be a student.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으로/로' 앞에 확인된 결과를 넣어 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the confirmed result before 으로/로.

explain_en: '확인하다' is you checking whether something is right; '확인되다' is the state after the result comes out. News, notices and reports often say '~로 확인됐다'. If it is not done yet, say '확인되지 않았어요' or use '미확인'.

p.n: 확인됐어요 means verified; 체크됐어요 means it was ticked on a list.
